ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 14316, promulgated on February 23, 2016, as amended), implemented through Korea Financial Intelligence Unit prudential regulations; Real Name Financial Transaction and Secret Protection Act (Act No. 6755, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 19097, as amended); FATF Recommendations 24 and 25; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Registry Extract (Certificate of Registered Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registry seal and officer signature; notarization of official translation; then Hague Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs; consular legalization is not applicable in this Apostille Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance and Corporate Existence Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean National Tax Service and local District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certification by issuing tax office and court registry; notarization; then Hague Apostille; no consular legalization step may be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Directors (corporate records signed by officer) and Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of corporate signatory identity and authority under Notary Act; then Hague Apostille; consular legalization is excluded.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public (authenticated form under Commercial Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication in Korean; sworn translation; Hague Apostille; consular legalization is parallel-only and not applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Commercial Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Bank operating in the Republic of Korea (corporate account-holding branch)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal and branch manager signature; notarization; then Hague Apostille; no consular legalization chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Director Identification and UBO Declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public on behalf of the shareholders/members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized affidavit of UBO; Hague Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs; consular legalization is not permissible for Apostille member states.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, officer, shareholder, authorized signatory and beneficial nominee must be screened against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, UK/EU consolidated lists, and domestic Korean disciplinary registries. Screening must be performed before submission, at incorporation, and every 180 days thereafter. Foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth corroboration, and, if any adverse indicator arises, the compliance officer must immediately file a suspicious transaction report with KFIU within 24 hours and consider terminating the engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (iRO) at https://www.iros.go.kr and the local district court registry name-clearance desk.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary corporate name must be written in Korean Hangul; English or other foreign scripts may be used only as a secondary transliteration appearing in the Articles of Association and board resolution. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a distinctive trading element or industry identifier, (2) an object clause complement describing the marine transport activity, (3) the statutory legal-form suffix "Yuhan Hoesa" (transliteration of limited company), and (4) the registered office city. Phonetic transliteration into Hangul must correspond to the intended English commercial name, and any divergence must be reconciled in the charter.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written reason citing similarity or statutory prohibition. Within 14 days, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the registry chief attaching a corrected or alternative name and comparative table showing distinctiveness. The registry has 5 business days to reply; if the rejection is based on similarity, a written consent from the existing name holder will cure the objection. The applicant may also reserve an alternative name concurrently. If the initial name reservation expires, a new application may be filed, and extensions are normally not available unless the delay results from pending ministerial approval or foreign apostille of the UBO declaration, in which case one 30-day extension may be sought with supporting evidence. A final denial may be challenged through a non-contentious civil application to the district court within 30 days of the rejection decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not wholly prohibited by the Korean Commercial Act for registration purposes, but it is generally rejected by the National Tax Service, customs authorities, and corporate banks for a Deep-Sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport enterprise. The Shipping Act and the Maritime Safety Act require an actual operational place of business in Korea from which the representative directs vessel operations, retains commercial records, and receives service of process. Banks and KFIU-regulated institutions treat a mere virtual office as a red flag under FATF Recommendation 24; therefore, the applicant must lease a physical office, display signage, employ at least one full-time local compliance administrator, and maintain crew and charter party records at that address before the corporate account can be opened.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) visible registered-office signage; (2) registered lease contract with deposit and monthly rental evidence; (3) electricity/telecommunications utility bill matching the office; (4) payroll and Korean social insurance records for local employees; (5) vessel registration or bareboat charter documents; (6) RORO bills of lading and port terminal invoices. Likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by district registry or municipal tax office in the first fiscal year is approximately 35%, increasing to 70% if the registry records list only a virtual office, and decreasing to 15% in subsequent years without tax or maritime safety triggers.

Statutory notarial tariff in the Notary Act, calculated on the aggregate member contribution; prevailing market benchmark approximately KRW 200,000 (USD 150-180).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 0.15-0.25 per Korean character; standard legal bundle fee USD 200-300.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Good Standing and tax clearance certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean National Tax Service and local District Court Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee per certificate (KRW 1,000-3,000) and certified copy fee; no professional service fee included.
Complimentary service for account-holding corporate customers; notarization and apostille costs are listed separately where applicable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287 through 287.74 and Articles 289, 292, 301, 317, 318 and 393; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 5 and 11; Maritime Transport Act and Ships Act for vessel operation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Relevant District Court Registry Office, Company Registration Division, in the judicial district where the Yuhan Hoesa registered office is located (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Corporation together with the Notarized Articles of Incorporation and all statutory attachments
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), but the capital shown in the Articles must be fully subscribed and paid or unconditionally committed before registration, evidenced by a verified Korean bank capital contribution certificate; no blocked escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: THAT this Yuhan Hoesa, duly subscribed and formed pursuant to the Korean Commercial Act, hereby adopts the Articles of Incorporation as its overriding corporate charter and confirms that the founding shareholders have subscribed to, and will remit before submission to the Registry Court, the total issued share capital in the amount stated in the capital contribution schedule. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution certificate, verifies the identity of each subscriber against the shareholders ledger, and directs the Chief Executive Officer to record the shareholding in the company register. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the Company shall open its principal operating account, along with any foreign currency account needed for deep-sea RoRo vehicle freight settlement, only at a bank authorized to operate in the Republic of Korea; the Representative Director, or any two directors acting jointly, are hereby authorized to execute all bank account forms, account mandates, remittance instructions, foreign exchange documents, freight collections and other instruments necessary for the lawful movement of corporate capital and operating revenue. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the registered office of the Company is established at the physical address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, which shall be the legal venue for service of process, court registry notices, tax communications and maritime regulatory correspondence, and shall not be changed except with an express subsequent board resolution and a duly amended registration. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT [Name A], appointed as Representative Director; [Name B], appointed as Executive Director; and [Name C], appointed as Statutory Auditor, each hereby accept office; the Representative Director is vested with full authority to represent the Company before the Korean court registry, National Tax Service, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Korean Coast Guard, authorized banks, classification societies and all other competent public agencies, and to execute and deliver the incorporation registration application, business registration application, deep-sea maritime cargo transport license application, ship registration documents and all customary maritime, environmental and safety instruments relating to the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the officers are instructed to cause the incorporation registration to be perfected within the statutory period and thereafter to obtain business registration, maritime transport licensing, Korean ship registration, SOLAS and MARPOL conformity certificates, and all environmental compliance documents as required by Korean law. Pending registration, no operational voyages shall be commenced, and the Company shall act only through the Representative Director in accordance with the Articles, the Commercial Act and any binding international convention adopted by the Republic of Korea. This resolution is effective immediately and may be presented to third parties as conclusive evidence of corporate authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Share Capital Subscription and Foreign Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea and an authorized foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of South Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholders must remit the proposed share capital into a domestic Korean bank account or into a temporary incorporation account opened at an authorized foreign exchange bank at least five banking days before the scheduled registry submission. Each subscriber must submit a statement of purpose, beneficial ownership identification, passport or corporate formation documents, bank power of attorney and a source-of-funds declaration. If any shareholder is a non-resident, the bank must prepare and retain the foreign investment notification and the remitter must satisfy the Foreign Investment Promotion Act by ensuring the overseas remittance is in Korean won or immediately converted through the bank dealing room. The bank must issue an official Korean-language capital contribution balance certificate, which the Registry Court accepts as proof of paid-in share capital; failure to complete this step blocks later court registration.
required_dossiers: Completed foreign investment notification or exemption checklist
Share subscription agreement and capital contribution schedule
Passport or corporate identification of each subscriber
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration
Overseas remittance instruction and foreign exchange receipt
Bank power of attorney and specimen signature card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags or suspends the remittance, cure the query by resubmitting corrected beneficiary or remitter information, provide an updated source-of-funds letter and ask the bank dealing room to repurchase the foreign currency; if KOTRA or the bank issues a formal foreign investment dispute, amend and reread the notification within five business days, and if necessary obtain a ministerial confirmation letter before reverting to the Registry Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization and Court Registration of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Court Registry Office (Company Registration Division) in the district of the Yuhan Hoesa registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation attorney must prepare Articles of Incorporation compliant with Articles 289 and 292 of the Korean Commercial Act, specifying the exact corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose that expressly includes deep-sea RoRo vehicle transportation, share capital, class of shares, number of shares, and the appointed directors and statutory auditor. Every incorporator must subscribe to and seal the Articles, after which the Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public who will verify the identity and authority of the signatories. The Representative Director or a duly appointed registration agent must then submit the notarized Articles, the court registration application, consent letters of officers, capital balance certificate, proof of registration tax and local education tax payment, and the representative director seal certificate to the Company Registration Division. The registry will verify statutory compliance, confirm the lawfulness of the corporate purpose, assign a corporate registration number and open the commercial register entry; no vessel operations may commence before this entry exists.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean original
Company registration application using court-prescribed form
Signed consents and usance declarations of all directors and auditor
Bank capital contribution certificate evidencing paid-in capital
Registration tax and education surtax payment receipt
Representative director seal certificate and legal power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry Court issues a request for correction, the exact defect must be cured within 14 days by amending the Articles, correcting tax payment calculation or supplying missing signatures; if the court suspends the application, the applicant may submit a supplementary memorandum under Commercial Act Article 317(3) or request a court-administered correction through the registry office. A false or incomplete seal may be remedied by obtaining a new notarial attestation and a clean seal certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Invoice System Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean National Tax Service Local District Tax Office and e-Tax Invoice HomeTax electronic window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after perfecting the court registration, the Representative Director or the appointed tax agent must file the Business Registration Application with the district tax office serving the registered office location, within one month of the court registration date. The application must be accompanied by the court-issued corporate registration certificate, certified copy of Articles, director identification cards, registered office lease contract, corporate seal certificate and a statement confirming the principal business code, in this case ISIC 5012 deep-sea water transport with RoRo vehicle handling. The tax office will issue the business registration certificate, which includes the corporate registration number used for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding tax, customs declarations and maritime freight invoicing. Immediately following issuance, the company must apply for e-Tax invoice issuance approval and register for the HomeTax collection system because all ocean freight invoices for vehicle shipments must be reported electronically under Korean VAT rules.
required_dossiers: Court-issued corporate registration extract and certificate
Business Registration Application Form 21
Director ID and resident registration copy or passport copy
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Principal business scope and estimated tariff classification statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local tax office returns a data mismatch notification, the company should submit the corrected lease, matching court registry extract and the director identity pages within seven days; if the HomeTax e-invoice registration stalls, the taxpayer should ask the tax office helpdesk for a manual approval order and, as a last resort, obtain jurisdictional written confirmation from the district tax commissioner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime Transport License, Korean Ship Registration and Vessel Safety Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (Maritime Transport Licensing Division), Korean Coast Guard Vessel Inspection Office and authorized classification society such as Korean Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court and tax registration, the company must apply to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for a Deep-Sea Maritime Cargo Transport Business License covering the RoRo car carrier route, vessel identity and intended voyage pattern. The application must include ownership or bareboat charter evidence, P&I insurance, hull and machinery insurance, tonnage certificate, ship management agreement if any, and a detailed RoRo stowage and lashing plan proving safe carriage of vehicles on enclosed vehicle decks. The Korean Coast Guard or delegated classification society must perform the initial SOLAS, Load Line and MARPOL survey for the vessel under the Ships Act and issue interim Safety Construction, Safety Equipment, International Oil Pollution Prevention, Air Pollution Prevention, Ballast Water Management, ISM Document of Compliance and Safety Management Certificate. For a Korean-flagged vessel, the ship must be entered into the Korean Ship Registration record and obtain a national certificate before commercial calls. The Maritime Transport Business License must be issued before any revenue voyage; the company must maintain a shore safety management office and designate a qualified Korean manager for ship operations.
required_dossiers: Deep-Sea Maritime Cargo Transport Business License application to MOF
Certificate of vessel ownership or valid bareboat charter agreement
Korean ship registration application and nationality certification
SOLAS Certificates, Load Line Certificate, MARPOL Annexes and IOPP Certificate or provisional classification certificates
P&I and H&M insurance certificates
ISM Document of Compliance and Safety Management Certificate
RoRo deck, ramp and lashing plan approved by a classification society
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOF or the Coast Guard issues a safety deficiency list, the company must submit a corrective safety management plan and request a re-inspection within 20 business days; if the Maritime Transport License is refused, the company may file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeals Act within 90 days and supplement the application with ship classification evidence or revised voyage plans; for delayed certificates, a temporary fitness letter may be obtained from the classification society while the statutory survey is completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Maritime Transport and Shipping Control Office and Korean Coast Guard Vessel Inspection Office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Deep-Sea Maritime Cargo Transport Business License; Certificate of Korean Ship Registration; SOLAS Safety Construction and Safety Equipment Certificates for RoRo Vehicle Carriers

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Marine Environmental Management Division of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for routine vessel operation; an Environmental Registration may be required only if shore-side RoRo terminal facilities, port works or vehicle holding areas are constructed or expanded. Vessel operations must nevertheless comply with the Marine Environment Management Act and MARPOL Convention certificates.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Marine fuel sulfur content must not exceed 0.50% m/m globally and 0.10% m/m in Korean port environs and controlled emission zones; machinery space oily water may be discharged only through an approved 15 ppm oil water separator compliant with MARPOL Annex I; ballast water must meet IMO D-2 standards with less than 10 viable organisms per cubic metre for organisms equal or greater than 50 micrometres and less than 10 viable organisms per millilitre for organisms between 10 and 50 micrometres; VOC emissions from fuel tank ventilation systems, if fitted, must be controlled under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 15; hazardous waste, used oils and cargo tank residues must be manifested and transported only by licensed Korean waste carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A Civil Defense fire safety permit is not applicable to the floating vessel itself, but the vessel must possess a Korean Coast Guard SOLAS fire safety certificate, structural fire protection certificate, load line certificate and approved cargo lashing plan. The shore administrative office must obtain a local fire department fire prevention and evacuation certification, and all Korean crew and shore staff must receive workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including vehicle ramp entry controls and RoRo deck risk training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal Home Tax Service (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr. Export declarations and customs clearance are processed through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) electronic UNI-PASS system at https://unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the unified TIN and VAT registration number is the Business Registration Number issued under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The company, through its legal representative or local tax agent, must file an Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office or domestic place of business, generally within 20 days from business commencement. Required submission documents include the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, register of directors, representative identification documents, proof of the domestic place of business such as a lease contract or ownership certificate, and for a foreign non-resident shareholder, a certificate of foreign incorporation and the foreign entities tax identification number. If a foreign non-resident entity has no domestic place of business but makes taxable supplies in Korea, it must appoint a Korean tax representative and register under the statutory simplified VAT registration procedures for foreign businesses before the taxable supply occurs. Upon successful review, the NTS issues the Business Registration Number, which also serves as the corporate entity TIN and the VAT ID. Amendments to business status, location, or representative must be filed with the NTS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide check-the-box classification elections or hybrid mismatch entity elections for a Yuhan Hoesa; a domestic corporation is mandatorily treated as an entity-level taxpayer under the Corporation Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary turnover threshold triggers VAT registration in Korea. VAT registration is mandatory for every business operator, including a Yuhan Hoesa, from the date taxable business activity commences in Korea. The optional simplified taxpayer regime for individual businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000 is not available to a limited liability company; therefore no KRW threshold applies for this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporations and all registered business operators in Korea must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS Home Tax System or through an NTS-approved electronic invoice service provider using API integration. Electronic tax invoice data must be transmitted to the National Tax Service under the statutory VAT filing schedule. Korea does not currently operate a real-time government fiscal clearance or anti-fraud stamping regime; instead, the NTS performs post-issuance electronic validation and cross-matching of buyer and seller VAT returns through the Hometax e-invoice database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value Added Tax Act, zero-rated supplies include exported goods and international transportation services by sea or air. A Yuhan Hoesa deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle carrier qualifies for the 0% VAT rate for the international ocean transport of vehicles, provided the supply is genuinely rendered in connection with international carriage and supported by documentary proof of the foreign supply, vessel movement, cargo carriage, and export or foreign exchange realization where applicable. Qualifying offshore digital services are not relevant to this maritime entity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration through UNI-PASS, together with the cargo loading report or ship s manifest for vehicles loaded in Korea

Original or electronic Bill of Lading (or sea waybill) issued by the Ro-Ro carrier showing vessel name, voyage number, VIN-level vehicle details, ports of loading and discharge, and the shipper and consignee
Commercial invoice and contract of carriage, charter party, or booking confirmation evidencing the international transport supply

Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation or a foreign exchange bank receipt issued in the Republic of Korea evidencing receipt of freight, charter hire, or export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Cargo manifest, port-call certificates, or ship agent certificates substantiating the actual international movement of the vehicles and the Ro-Ro voyage
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will scrutinize any zero-rating claim against the VAT return, jury invoices, customs declaration database, vessel movement records, and foreign exchange receipt records. If the required export documentation or foreign exchange realization evidence is missing or unverifiable, the NTS may disallow the zero-rating retroactively, assess 10% VAT on the supply value, claw back any previously refunded input VAT, and impose statutory additional tax penalties for underreporting, unfounded refunds, or failure to preserve supporting evidence. Fraudulent or deliberately false zero-rating claims can also lead to criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment or monetary penalties, together with enhanced civil penalty rates on the suppressed tax base.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (central bank) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with operational execution through Authorized Foreign Exchange Banks and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly liberalised but statutorily monitored foreign exchange system. Current account transactions, including international ocean freight income derived from Ro-Ro vehicle transport and ordinary operating expenses, can generally be executed without pre-approval, subject to mandatory reporting to the Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The Korean won is freely convertible on the current account, and there is no requirement to surrender export proceeds into KRW; the entity may retain foreign currency receipts in designated Foreign Exchange Deposit Accounts. Capital account convertibility remains more conditional: equity injections, shareholder loans, and cross-border financial arrangements by foreign residents require declaration or prior approval in specified cases, but ordinary repatriation of dividends and profits by foreign-invested companies is permitted after corporate tax settlement. Profit remittance hurdles typically involve submission of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, board resolutions authorising the dividend, and the filing of the corresponding foreign exchange transaction report. In practice, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires all resident-nonresident settlements above prescribed thresholds to pass through a domestic Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank, which makes a local banking relationship indispensable for compliant treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds, including ocean freight earnings from non-resident charterers and cargo interests for Ro-Ro transportation services, must be collected and settled through an Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank within the statutory settlement period, generally 180 days from the date of service completion or the contractual payment date stated in the bill of lading or freight invoice unless a longer period is approved by the bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio; the company may retain the entire foreign currency export receipt in a Foreign Exchange Deposit Account. All receipts must be reported in FEIS through the authorised bank, and the payment must be supported by freight invoices, charter party agreements, and vessel operational documentation to evidence the underlying current account transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Exchange Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Export Proceeds Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange Deposit Account / Trade Settlement Services Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise Business, Revolut, Payoneer, and similar non-bank international money service businesses are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission of Korea as domestic financial institutions and are not Authorized Foreign Exchange Banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Consequently, they cannot lawfully service the treasury settlement and FEIS reporting obligations of a Korean resident corporate entity. They may be used only as auxiliary payment cards or collection wallets outside Korea, but all statutory KRW and foreign currency settle-governance, including freight receipt collection, capital injection, and FX hedging, must be executed through a domestic Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank. Relying on a fintech EMI as the primary clearing rail would create regulatory non-compliance and immediate underwriting rejection at the bank onboarding stage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa engaging in cross-border shipping, at least one representative director or a lawful attorney-in-fact must physically appear at a domestic branch of the Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank to complete corporate account opening and real-name verification. Foreign non-resident directors who are not present in Korea generally cannot open a full operational and foreign exchange account through a purely remote digital process. A remote video interview may supplement the application, but it does not replace the physical presence requirement for corporate entities with significant cross-border capital flows. Consular proxy opening may be permitted only after pre-approval by the bank compliance committee and after the nominated proxy appears in person at the Korean branch carrying a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, the company formation documents, corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, and the beneficial owner’s verified identity documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership opacity and nominee shareholding red flags in the Korean corporate register and payment chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract of the Korean company registration register, notarised shareholder ledger, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration signed by each natural person holding more than 25% of the equity, passport copies of all UBOs, recent utility bill or bank reference for each UBO, and, if any nominee structure is used, the original nomination trust deed accompanied by source-of-wealth evidence for the underlying beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the claimed Ro-Ro shipping business scope and the initial capital injection source, particularly for large capital receipts from foreign jurisdictions with no visible nexus to vessel ownership, chartering, or maritime operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements for each investing shareholder, wire instruction confirmations, tax clearance or entity standing certificate from the source jurisdiction, an executed vessel purchase agreement, bareboat charter or financing term sheet, a standard Formation Bill of Lading or ocean freight contract, audit-ready financial projections, the foreign investment declaration filed with the authorized bank or KOTRA, and a net worth statement signed by each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade embargo screening hits on the vessel operator, sister ships, UBOs, or chartering counterparties due to port call history or vessel flag registrations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions and adverse-news screening report against UN, EU, OFAC, and KFTC lists covering all UBOs and vessel counterparties; vessel IMO number and flag registration certificate; International Ship and Port Facility Security Certificate; Port State Control inspection records for the preceding 12 months; a full charter party agreement; the vessel owner’s compliance manual; and a written statement confirming no calls at sanctioned ports or ship-to-ship transfers with blacklisted vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign exchange reporting concerns, specifically unreported foreign currency receipts or misclassification of ocean freight proceeds in the prior transaction profile of the shareholders, directors, or affiliated shipping lines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FEIS transaction history report from any existing Korean banking relationships, audited financial statements of the entity and connected entities, receivable aging report tied to ocean bills of lading and freight invoices, charter broker confirmation letters, classification of each cross-border payment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and a formal memorandum from an accredited Korean certified public accountant confirming the accuracy and completeness of all required foreign exchange declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injection must be executed through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route. The company first files a foreign investment declaration at a designated domestic bank or KOTRA, receives a foreign investment registration acknowledgment, and then the shareholder transmits funds via SWIFT MT103 into a dedicated Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account at the Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank. The remittance must use the FEIS purpose code designated for foreign direct investment equity subscription and not a general loan or trade purpose code. After the funds are credited and the bank issues a capital entry/verification certificate, a licensed certified public accountant conducts paid-in capital verification based on the corporate registry amendment for the capital increase or initial incorporation. Once verified, the funds may be used for working capital, vessel acquisition payments, charter deposits, and operational expenses; transfer of the balance to a general operating account is recorded as a foreign-exchange-purpose disclosed transaction for FEIS and tax reporting.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade and operational disbursements, the primary clearing rails are direct telegraphic transfers under SWIFT MT103 from the corporate foreign exchange account, with the FEIS purpose code reflecting ocean freight expenses, charter hire, vessel repair and maintenance, port costs, bunker fuel procurement, or crew wages as applicable. A Commercial Letter of Credit can be used for procurement of vessel spare parts, equipment, or yard refurbishment services, with KIFFA or UCP600 rules governing the presentation of shipping documents. Documentary Collections are appropriate for certain seller-draft transactions tied to marine services, allowing the bank to transmit documents against payment or acceptance. For Korean won operating payments to domestic counterparties, the company may use standard KRW current account transfers, but any conversion from retained foreign currency receivables must be executed as a spot FX trade with the Authorized Foreign Exchange Bank and reported under the relevant current account purpose code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax plus Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the local municipal tax office (Si/Gun/Gu) where the principal office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the end of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due on or before 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return triggers an additional tax of 20% of the assessed corporate income tax, increased to 40% if the return remains unfiled for more than six months; unpaid tax accrues interest at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum); prolonged non-payment or non-filing can result in asset seizure by the NTS and administrative enforcement procedures leading to mandatory closure/dissolution of the enterprise

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Enterprise Management Report (Annual Performance and Beneficial Ownership Report for Foreign-Invested Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE), filed through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) integrated foreign investment management portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, in practice by 31 March for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or fraudulent filing attracts an administrative fine of up to KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500); the foreign investment registration may be revoked, and all income tax exemptions, cash grants, and support benefits under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) may be cancelled

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Submission (only if the statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, and the National Tax Service (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audited financial statements must be presented to the annual meeting of members within three months after fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a 31 December year-end) and, once approved, the audit report must be filed with FSS/DART within two weeks of the approval date, in any case no later than 15 April for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of a mandatory external audit or late filing allows the Financial Services Commission to designate a certified public accounting (CPA) firm at the company's expense and impose an administrative fine of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 38,000); the company's tax return using unaudited financial statements is treated as defective, triggering additional tax penalties; repeated violations may lead to prosecutorial indictment and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Fleet and Transportation Performance Report for the Deep-Sea Ro-Ro Ocean Car Carrier Licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), Maritime Industry Licensing Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year operator); the underlying marine transport licence is issued for a fixed term and must be renewed no later than 60 days before its expiry (ordinarily every five years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual performance report is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 10,000,000 under the Marine Transportation Act; non-renewal of the licence results in automatic forfeiture of the operating licence and removal of the vessel from the official registry of international ocean-going carriers, effectively prohibiting the Ro-Ro vessel from lawfully entering or departing Korean waters

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Confirmation and Commercial Registry Update (Members, Directors, Charges, Minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean District Court Commercial Registration Office (Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in registered particulars (registered office, directors, members, or capital/contribution amount) must be registered with the court within two weeks of the change; the annual confirmation of the statutory registers is completed at the ordinary meeting of members within three months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false registration triggers a non-compliance fine (Kwon-Go-Ta-Ryo) of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) under the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act; persistent failure to maintain accurate registers can expose the company to a court order for compulsory dissolution, and the directors may be subject to personal liability for resulting damages

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Other Companies (Article 2), a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) must retain an independent certified public accountant (CPA) for a statutory external audit if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year: (a) total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 or more (approximately USD 9,200,000); (b) total assets of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more together with total operating revenue of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more for two consecutive years; (c) it is classified as a public-interest company under Article 2(2) of the same Act (listed company, financial institution, or a company designated by the Financial Services Commission), irrespective of size; or (d) a Korean court or the Financial Services Commission orders an audit because the company is deemed to jeopardise creditors or public interest, for example by relying on state maritime subsidies or external financing. All audits must be performed by a CPA registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA), and the audit opinion must address compliance with the Korean Accounting Standards and the Korean Statutory Audit Standards that adopt the International Standards on Auditing (ISA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) if the company is listed, a financial institution, or otherwise meets the mandatory K-IFRS criteria; non-public Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards. Because the company is engaged in international maritime Ro-Ro transport, it may also elect the Tonnage Tax regime, which requires audited financial statements in accordance with the Special Tax Treatment Control Act and the tax accounting standards applicable to international shipping companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information of the Yuhan Hoesa is reported annually to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Foreign Investment Enterprise Management Report, due on 31 March for calendar-year filers, where the foreign investor owns 10% or more of the company. Any transfer of membership interest that changes the foreign investor's equity ratio must be reported to MOTIE within 30 days of the transfer date under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Domestically, the company must maintain up-to-date statutory registers at its registered office; there is no separate public annual beneficial-ownership return for unlisted Korean limited liability companies, but the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) may require disclosure of beneficial owners in the course of AML examinations, and financial institutions will require current UBO certificates when the company opens or maintains bank accounts for wire transfers and Swift letters of credit. The transfer of a membership interest to a third party requires the consent of all members unless otherwise stated in the articles of incorporation, and the transfer must be reflected in the members register and filed with the commercial registry within two weeks of the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax headline rate, producing an effective 26.4% rate after the 10% local income tax surcharge; the progressive national brackets are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International maritime transport may elect the tonnage-basis corporate tax regime under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, which substitutes notional profit per net tonnage for actual accounting profit; Free Economic Zone foreign direct investment can receive a 5-year 100% and subsequent 2-year 50% national and local tax holiday; R&D and facility investment tax credits, foreign tax credits, and indirect foreign tax credits for overseas dividends are available; the RoRo ocean car-carrier business should review eligibility for the Korean shipping tonnage tax election before filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal, with the local income tax surcharge schedule included in the same electronic filing package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, with a mandatory interim prepayment for fiscal years longer than six months; calendar-year taxpayers generally make interim payments by the last day of the month following the one-year half.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year entity, the final Corporate Income Tax Return must be filed no later than 31 March of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, the deadline is the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end, extended to the next business day when the deadline falls on a holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1: Entity Identification and Corporate Type
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name KR_YUHANGHOESA, business registration number, head office or main place of business address, representative director, statutory tax classification as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), principal business code corresponding to ISIC 5012 / NAICS 483111 deep-sea RoRo vehicle transport, and whether the corporation is a resident domestic corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a resident corporation, it must declare its worldwide income; identify non-resident ultimate shareholders with names and tax residences so that the later dividend withholding and DTA schedules can be reconciled, and do not classify the Korean entity as a non-resident branch when it is the contracting carrier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Business Year, Return Type, and Special Elections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record the fiscal year beginning and end dates, check whether the filing is a final return, provisional return, or amended return, and identify any special election such as the tonnage tax election for international maritime transport or tax treaty exemption/reduction elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A RoRo carrier electing the tonnage tax must provide vessel ownership, net tonnage, and foreign-trade route details; if the election is not made, the general corporate tax computation using audited accounting income will apply, and all non-resident related-party transactions must be cross-referenced to the transfer pricing schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Reconciliation from Accounting Net Income to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start from accounting net income per Korean IFRS or generally accepted accounting principles and add back non-deductible expenses such as corporate income tax, penalties, entertainment excess, donation excess, and non-deductible depreciation, while subtracting non-taxable income such as dividend received deductions from qualifying domestic subsidiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the Korean LLC pays charter hire, voyage costs, or management fees to non-resident related parties, the add-back section must be reviewed for transfer pricing adjustments; a controlled transaction below arm's length must be adjusted upward to the arm's-length amount, and the adjustment must be reflected in the tax base rather than allowed to escape through non-deductible expense recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4: Deductions, Tax Loss Carryforward, and Tax-Exempt Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter allowable losses carried forward from prior years, statutory tax-exempt income, qualifying tax credits carried forward, and all applicable deductions under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ten-year general loss carryforward and the fifteen-year SME extension if the Korean entity qualifies; if the entity previously accumulated losses while controlled by non-resident owners, substantiate the continuity and identity-of-business requirement to prevent the tax office from reclassifying the carryforward as a transaction designed solely to obtain a tax benefit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5: Tax Base, Progressive Tax Rates, and Headline Corporate Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable income after all reconciling entries, apply the applicable progressive corporate tax rate bracket, and compute the national corporate income tax before credits; where the tonnage tax election is valid, substitute the tonnage-derived taxable income for accounting-derived income and compute the corresponding national tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax base must include gross Korean-sourced ocean freight income from RoRo vehicle transport; if the voyage is international and all cargo is carried between foreign ports, correctly apply Korean shipping-source rules and DTA permanent establishment rules rather than excluding the income without a statutory basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6: Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credit, and Withholding Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter foreign tax credits, foreign dividend deduction credits, R&D credits, facility investment credits, employment credits, and any prepayments or interim corporate tax payments made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For profits earned from an overseas feeder network or foreign agency structure, claim foreign tax credit only with a Tax Residency Certificate and evidence that the foreign levy was legally imposed; the same schedule should cross-check Korean withholding on any interest, dividend, or royalty paid during the year to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Non-Resident Remittance and Withholding Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all payments to non-residents during the year, including dividends, interest, royalties, charter-hire payments, ocean freight commissions, technical service fees, and management fees, together with the amount withheld at source and the withholding tax rate applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the critical box for the RoRo LLC: if dividends are to be remitted to a non-resident owner, the statutory 20% corporate income tax withholding plus the 10% local surcharge must be declared, unless a DTA application for a reduced rate has been properly made with the counterparty Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement; omitting this box triggers fraud penalties and can expose directors to personal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Total Tax Payable, Local Surtax, and Payment Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute final national corporate income tax, add the 10% local income tax surcharge, deduct interim payments already made, and state the balance due or refund requested; include the date by which the balance must be paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local surcharge is calculated on the national corporate tax liability, including the national tax after treaty reduction; any dividend distribution covered by treaty should show the reduced national tax and corresponding local surcharge so that the effective 22% statutory withholding is not erroneously reduced by treaty without a valid application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing, failure to file, or failure to pay triggers the Framework Act on National Taxes penalty regime: 20% negligence tax for underreporting or non-reporting in the absence of fraud, and 40% for fraudulent underreporting, plus a daily delinquency surcharge until the tax is paid; criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act can lead to imprisonment of up to three years and a fine of up to ten times the evaded tax, with border-control blacklisting and asset freezing in serious offshore evasion cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% corporate income tax withholding plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax withheld, making the effective statutory withholding rate 22% on gross dividends paid by the Korean Yuhan Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder without a Korean permanent establishment; treaty rates of 5% or 10% may apply depending on the DTA and the ownership threshold.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the Korean payer and the non-resident recipient must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the competent tax authority of the recipient jurisdiction; (ii) obtain a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that the non-resident is the ultimate owner and not an agent, nominee, or conduit; (iii) submit the Nonresident Income Tax Exemption or Reduction Application through the NTS HomeTax portal or to the local district tax office before or at the time of the withholding remittance; (iv) retain the DTA article analysis, shareholding or loan documentation, and evidence of substance such as board resolutions, bank accounts, and employees for the RoRo shipping structure; and (v) if a reduced rate is not pre-approved or is denied, withhold the statutory 22%, remit it by the monthly withholding deadline, and file a tax refund claim within the applicable statutory claims period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound interest and royalties is also 20% national tax plus 10% local surcharge, for an effective 22% rate; most Korean DTA reduce interest to 10% or 15% and royalties to 10% or 15%, subject to the recipient being the beneficial owner and the payment not being attributable to a Korean permanent establishment; intercompany charter hire for vessels is generally treated as freight or leasing income, not royalty, and must be separately analyzed under the DTA profits-from-shipping article.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is mandatory when annual cross-border related-party transactions reach KRW 100 billion; Local File is mandatory when the same transactions reach KRW 50 billion; and additional documentation is required when transactions with a related party resident in a tax haven reach KRW 30 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but it applies substance-over-form doctrine through the GAAR in Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and through the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs; for a deep-sea RoRo vehicle carrier, Core Income-Generating Activities include vessel ownership or chartering, flag registration, commercial management, cargo booking, crewing, bunkering, and maintenance decisions, and a Korean Yuhan Hoesa claiming tonnage tax or treaty benefits must demonstrate real management and operations in Korea rather than acting as a shell or nominee for non-resident principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating RoRo freight revenue, recording below-market charter-hire contracts with a non-resident related party, fabricating bunker or port expenses, or omitting the Korean withholding obligation on dividends remitted to a non-resident shareholder in order to reduce Korean corporate income tax and escape foreign dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act authorizes imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to ten times the amount of evaded tax; the Framework Act on National Taxes applies a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty and a 20% negligent understatement penalty, plus daily delinquency surcharges until the amount is paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced when the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a sham vehicle or a mere instrumentality, making directors jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and civil restitution; the NTS may blacklist the directors, impose travel bans, freeze personal assets, and criminal conviction will result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany cross-border transactions with non-resident shipowners, brokers, agents, or treasury affiliates are priced deviating from the arm's-length standard, or the Korean LLC fails to prepare and provide the Master File, Local File, and tax-haven transaction file after crossing the KRW 100 billion, KRW 50 billion, or KRW 30 billion statutory thresholds, thereby distorting the Korean taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs permits the NTS to re-determine the arm's-length price, adjust taxable income, and impose penalty taxes together with non-payment surcharges; the Framework Act on National Taxes further imposes up to 20% understatement penalties, or 40% if the TP misstatement is fraudulent, and denial of the deduction for the excessive portion of the controlled payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false transfer pricing documentation are treated as active participants in the offshore tax scheme; they can be held personally liable for the additional corporate tax and penalties, subjected to NTS blacklisting and travel restrictions, and prosecuted criminally for falsification of tax documents and attempted tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Economic Substance Deficit, and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa has no substantive entity management, no local vessel fleet, no crew employment, no board meetings in Korea, and no local commercial decisions, but is used to hold RoRo vessel income and to claim treaty benefits, tonnage tax, or profit-repatriation advantages for a non-resident parent; alternatively, the structure engages in treaty shopping through a conduit jurisdiction with no business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The GAAR under Article 17 of the Framework Act on National Taxes allows the tax authorities to disregard the sham entity and attribute the income to the true controlling person; the Principal Purpose Test under Korea's tax treaties and the OECD Multilateral Instrument denies treaty relief; the omitted or mischaracterized income is subject to the 40% fraud penalty and statutory interest charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts and tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and impose joint and several liability on the directors and shadow directors who exercised actual control; remedies include civil restitution of diverted corporate assets, personal bank account seizure, NTS blacklisting, travel ban, and a term of imprisonment for criminal tax evasion arising from the sham structure.
